column1: discontinuance§The discontinuance of the ferry left three islands with no winter service and no plan for replacing it.§渡轮的**停运**让三座岛屿冬季没有航班，也没有替代方案。§dis-（否定）+ continue（继续）
discontinuity§A discontinuity in the record between 1938 and 1946 makes the long-term trend impossible to state with confidence.§1938 至 1946 年间记录的**中断**使得长期趋势无法有把握地陈述。§
discord§Discord over one paragraph split a committee that had agreed on everything else in eleven months of work.§围绕一个段落的**不和**分裂了一个在十一个月工作中其余事项全都一致的委员会。§dis-（分开）+ cord（心，同 cordial 诚恳的）→ 心不齐
discourteous§It would be discourteous to leave before the speeches, and roughly forty people did exactly that.§在致辞前离场是**失礼的**，而大约四十人正是这么干的。§dis-（否定）+ courteous（有礼的）
discredit§One fabricated footnote discredited a book whose remaining nine hundred pages have never been challenged.§一条捏造的脚注**败坏**了一本书的声誉，而其余九百页从未受到质疑。§dis-（否定）+ credit（信用）
discreet§Her inquiries were discreet enough that the man being investigated recommended her for a promotion.§她的查访**审慎**到被调查的那个人还推荐了她升职。§dis-（分开）+ cre ← cern（分辨，同 discern 辨别）
discrepancy§The discrepancy is eleven thousand units, and neither warehouse can explain where they went.§这个**差异**是一万一千件，两个仓库都说不清它们去了哪里。§dis-（分开）+ crep（响）→ 对不上、响声不一
discrete§The stages are discrete in the textbook and continuous in every patient anyone has actually treated.§这些阶段在教科书里是**离散分立的**，在任何实际治疗过的病人身上都是连续的。§dis-（分开）+ cret（分辨，同 secret 秘密）
discretion§The rule leaves the decision to the officer's discretion, and outcomes vary by district more than by case.§规则把决定权交给警员的**自由裁量**，结果因辖区而异的程度超过因案情而异。§
discretionary§The discretionary fund exists for emergencies and has spent the last four years paying for routine repairs.§这笔**可自由支配的**基金本为应急而设，过去四年却在支付日常维修。§
discriminating§A discriminating buyer would have noticed the varnish, which is nine decades younger than the paint beneath it.§**眼光挑剔的**买家会注意到那层清漆——它比底下的颜料年轻九十年。§dis-（分开）+ crimin（分辨，同 crime 罪／判定）
disdain§Her disdain for the format was obvious, and she answered every question in one sentence to prove it.§她对这种形式的**鄙夷**显而易见，为此她用一句话回答每个问题。§dis-（否定）+ dain ← dign（有价值，同 dignity 尊严）→ 认为不值
disenchant§Two years inside the ministry disenchanted him completely, and he now writes about it for a living.§在部里的两年让他彻底**幻灭**，如今他靠写这件事谋生。§dis-（去掉）+ enchant（迷住）
disgruntle§The new rota disgruntled everyone on nights, and three of the best nurses resigned within a month.§新的排班表**惹恼**了所有上夜班的人，三名最好的护士一个月内辞职。§dis-（加强）+ gruntle（哼哼，同 grunt 咕哝）
disguise§The building's real purpose was hidden behind the disguise of a laundry that took in almost no laundry.§这栋楼的真实用途藏在一家几乎不收衣物的洗衣店的**伪装**背后。§dis-（去掉）+ guise（外表）
dishearten§The rejection did not dishearten her, and she sent the same manuscript out again the following Tuesday.§这次退稿并没有**使她气馁**，下周二她又把同一份稿子寄了出去。§dis-（去掉）+ heart（心）
dishevel§The wind disheveled her notes across the platform, and she read the lecture out of order for forty minutes.§风把她的讲稿**吹得凌乱**散落一站台，她乱着顺序讲了四十分钟。§
disillusion§Nothing disillusions a new teacher faster than discovering how much of the job is paperwork.§没有什么比发现这份工作有多少是文书更快地让新教师**幻想破灭**。§dis-（去掉）+ illusion（幻觉）
disincline§The experience disinclined him to volunteer again, though he never said so to the people who had asked.§这段经历让他**不愿**再当志愿者，尽管他从未对邀请他的人这么说过。§dis-（否定）+ incline（倾向）
disingenuous§The answer was disingenuous rather than false: every word was true and the impression was the opposite of the facts.§这个回答是**虚伪**而非虚假的——字字属实，给人的印象却与事实相反。§dis-（否定）+ ingenuous（率真的）
disjoint§The two halves of the report are disjoint: the analysis never uses the data the first section spent forty pages collecting.§报告的两半是**脱节的**——分析部分从未用到前半部分花四十页收集的数据。§dis-（分开）+ joint（关节）
dislodge§No argument dislodged him from a position he had taken before reading the evidence.§没有任何论辩能把他从一个他在读证据之前就已选定的立场上**撼动**。§dis-（离开）+ lodge（安置）
dismantle§They dismantled the reactor over nine years, and the final component left the site in an unmarked truck.§他们用九年**拆解**了这座反应堆，最后一个部件由一辆无标识卡车运离厂区。§dis-（去掉）+ mantle（斗篷）→ 一层层剥开
dismay§To the dismay of the trustees, the auditor's letter arrived on the morning of the fundraising dinner.§令理事们**沮丧**的是，审计师的信在募款晚宴当天早上寄到了。§dis-（否定）+ may（力量，同 might 力量）→ 没了底气
dismissal§The dismissal was found unfair on procedural grounds, and the compensation cost the firm four times his salary.§这次**解雇**因程序问题被判不公，赔偿花掉公司相当于他四倍薪水的钱。§
dismissive§His dismissive reply to a junior colleague was forwarded eleven times and reached the chief executive by lunchtime.§他对一位年轻同事**轻慢的**回复被转发了十一次，午饭前就到了首席执行官那里。§
disorient§The identical corridors disorient every visitor, and the hospital eventually painted each floor a different colour.§一模一样的走廊**让每位访客迷失方向**，医院最终把每层楼刷成不同颜色。§dis-（否定）+ orient（定向／东方）
disparage§Reviewers disparaged the technique for years, and the same reviewers now describe it as standard practice.§评论者**贬损**这项技术多年，如今同一批人称它是标准做法。§dis-（否定）+ parage（同等身份，同 peer 同侪）→ 说人不配
disparager§Her chief disparager was a man whose own results had failed to replicate three times.§她最主要的**诋毁者**是一个自己的结果三次未能重复出来的人。§
disparate§The two datasets are too disparate to combine: one measures households, the other measures buildings.§这两套数据**差异太大**，无法合并——一套测量家庭，另一套测量建筑。§dis-（分开）+ par（相等，同 par 平价）
disparity§The disparity between the two schools is not in teaching but in what happens after three in the afternoon.§两所学校之间的**差距**不在教学，而在下午三点之后发生的事。§
dispassionate§A dispassionate account of the accident took four years to produce and satisfied neither family.§一份**冷静客观**的事故记述花了四年才写成，两家人都不满意。§dis-（否定）+ passion（激情）

dispatch§Headquarters dispatched two engineers on a nine-hour flight to reset a switch the local staff could not find.§总部**派遣**两名工程师坐九小时飞机去重置一个当地员工找不到的开关。§dis-（离开）+ patch ← pact（束缚，同 impede 阻碍）→ 解开束缚放出去
dispel§The photographs dispelled a rumour that four official denials had only made more credible.§这些照片**驱散**了一个被四次官方否认反而弄得更可信的传闻。§dis-（分开）+ pel（推，同 propel 推进）
dispersal§The dispersal of seeds by a single bird species keeps nine kinds of tree alive on this island.§靠一种鸟**散播**种子，这座岛上九种树才得以存活。§
disperse§Police dispersed the crowd in eleven minutes, and the inquiry into how they did it took eleven months.§警方十一分钟就**驱散**了人群，而调查他们如何做到的用了十一个月。§dis-（分开）+ spers（撒，同 sparse 稀疏的）
dispersive§The medium is dispersive, so a pulse that leaves sharp arrives smeared across several microseconds.§这种介质是**色散的**，因此出发时锐利的脉冲抵达时被抹开成好几微秒。§
displace§The dam displaced eleven villages, and the compensation scheme reached about a third of the households.§这座大坝**迫使**十一个村庄迁移，补偿方案覆盖了大约三分之一的家庭。§dis-（离开）+ place（位置）
display§The museum displays four percent of what it owns, and the rest sits in a warehouse forty miles away.§这家博物馆**展出**其藏品的百分之四，其余存放在四十英里外的仓库里。§
disposable§Treating staff as disposable worked while hiring was easy, and stopped working the year hiring was not.§把员工当作**用完即弃的**在招人容易时行得通，在招人不易的那年就不行了。§
disposition§His disposition to check everything twice slowed the team down and caught the error that would have ended it.§他事事复核两遍的**性情**拖慢了团队，也逮到了那个本会终结团队的错误。§dis-（分开）+ posit（放置，同 position 位置）→ 心思的摆法
disputation§The disputation lasted three days and settled nothing, which was more or less the expected outcome.§这场**论战**持续三天，什么也没解决，这多少是意料之中的结果。§
disputatious§The most disputatious member of the panel was also the only one who had read the underlying study.§评审组里最**好争辩的**成员，也是唯一读过原始研究的人。§
disregard§Complete disregard for the maintenance schedule went unnoticed for nine years and unpunished afterward.§对维护计划的完全**无视**九年未被察觉，此后也未受处罚。§dis-（否定）+ regard（关注）
disrepute§The clinic fell into disrepute after a single television programme, and the closure followed within a year.§这家诊所在一档电视节目后**名声扫地**，一年内就关了门。§dis-（否定）+ repute（名声）
disrupt§One faulty relay disrupted service for two hundred thousand people during the four busiest hours of the week.§一个故障继电器在一周中最繁忙的四小时里**中断**了二十万人的服务。§dis-（分开）+ rupt（断裂，同 interrupt 打断）
dissembler§The dissembler was caught by a detail he could not have faked: the dates on a parking ticket.§这个**伪装者**栽在一个他无法伪造的细节上——一张停车罚单上的日期。§dis-（否定）+ semble（相似，同 resemble 相似）→ 装得不像自己
disseminate§The findings were disseminated to nine hundred clinics, and eleven of them changed practice within the year.§这些发现被**传播**到九百家诊所，其中十一家在一年内改变了做法。§dis-（分开）+ semin（种子，同 seminar 研讨班）→ 播种出去
dissemination§Dissemination was the easy half; persuading anyone to act on it took another six years.§**传播**是容易的那一半，说服人据此行动又花了六年。§
dissension§Dissension inside the coalition became public in April, and the government fell before the end of June.§联盟内部的**纷争**在四月公开化，政府在六月底前垮台。§dis-（分开）+ sens ← sent（感觉，同 sense 感觉）→ 想法不一
dissipate§The advantage dissipated within two quarters once three competitors copied the feature and undercut the price.§三个竞争对手一模仿这项功能又压低价格，这项优势两个季度内就**消散**殆尽。§dis-（分开）+ sip ← sup（抛）→ 抛散掉

dissolute§His dissolute decade is the part everyone quotes, and the twenty disciplined years afterward are the part that mattered.§他**放荡**的那十年是人人引用的部分，而之后二十年的自律才是真正要紧的。§dis-（分开）+ solut（松开，同 solve 解决）→ 全然放开
dissolve§Parliament was dissolved in March, and the election that followed returned almost exactly the same members.§议会于三月**解散**，随后的选举送回了几乎完全相同的一批议员。§
distaste§Her distaste for self-promotion cost her two jobs and won her the trust of everyone she worked with.§她对自我推销的**反感**让她丢了两份工作，也赢得了每个共事者的信任。§dis-（否定）+ taste（口味）
distillation§The essay is a distillation of nine years of notes into fourteen pages that anyone can read.§这篇文章是九年笔记的**提炼**，浓缩成任何人都读得懂的十四页。§de-（向下）+ still（滴，同 still 蒸馏器）→ 一滴滴滴出精华
distinct§There are two distinct problems here, and the plan solves the easier one while claiming to solve both.§这里有两个**截然不同的**问题，而方案解决了较容易的那个，却声称两个都解决了。§dis-（分开）+ stinct（刺，同 instinct 本能）→ 刺出分界
distort§The lens distorts anything near the edge, which is why the building appears to lean in every photograph.§这枚镜头会**扭曲**靠近边缘的一切，所以那栋楼在每张照片里都显得倾斜。§dis-（分开）+ tort（扭，同 torture 折磨）
distortion§The distortion was introduced in translation: the original says "unlikely," and the English version says "impossible."§这处**曲解**是在翻译中产生的——原文说「不太可能」，英文版说「不可能」。§
distract§A single notification distracts the reader for about twenty seconds and costs another two minutes to recover.§一条通知会让读者**分心**约二十秒，再花两分钟才能恢复。§dis-（分开）+ tract（拉，同 attract 吸引）→ 把注意力拉走
distraction§Distraction, not difficulty, is why the chapter took three weeks: the work itself needed about nine hours.§让这一章拖了三周的是**分心**而非难度——工作本身约需九小时。§
distribution§The distribution is skewed enough that the average tells you almost nothing about a typical household.§这个**分布**偏斜得厉害，平均值几乎无法告诉你典型家庭的情况。§
diversify§The farm diversified after the third bad year, and the mix of crops has carried it through two droughts since.§第三个歉收年后农场开始**多元化经营**，此后作物组合让它熬过了两次干旱。§divers（不同）+ fy（使）
diversion§The diversion of the stream solved one village's flooding and created another's two miles downstream.§这条溪流的**改道**解决了一个村子的水患，又在下游两英里处制造了另一个。§di-（离开）+ vers（转，同 reverse 倒转）
diversity§The diversity of the collection is its value: nine hundred varieties, most of them grown nowhere else.§这批种质的**多样性**正是它的价值——九百个品种，多数别处不种。§
divert§Traffic was diverted through a village of four hundred people for eleven months of roadworks.§因十一个月的道路施工，车流被**改道**穿过一个四百人的村子。§
divisive§The proposal was divisive inside the party and barely noticed outside it, which is the usual pattern.§这项提案在党内**引起分裂**，党外几乎无人注意，这是常有的情形。§divis（分开，同 divide 分割）
